<?php
$eps = 1e-8;
$INF = 2000000000;

$l = 0;
$r = 0;
$ans = 0;
$q = 0;
$Q = 0;
$p = 0;
$w = array_fill(0, 99, false);
$W = array_fill(0, 99, false);

// Read input
$input = trim(fgets(STDIN));
if ($input === false) {
    exit(0);
}
$parts = preg_split('/\s+/', $input);
if (count($parts) < 2) {
    exit(0);
}
$l = (int)$parts[0];
$r = (int)$parts[1];

// Convert l to binary digits (LSB first)
while ($l > 0) {
    $w[$q++] = ($l % 2 === 1);
    $l = intdiv($l, 2);
}

// Convert r to binary digits (LSB first)
while ($r > 0) {
    $W[$Q++] = ($r % 2 === 1);
    $r = intdiv($r, 2);
}

// Find the highest bit position where w and W differ
for ($i = $Q; $i >= 0; $i--) {
    if ($w[$i] !== $W[$i]) {
        $p = $i + 1;
        break;
    }
}

// Calculate answer: 2^p - 1
$ans = (1 << $p) - 1;

echo $ans;
?>

<?php
$eps = 1e-8;

}

        break;
    }
}

?>

<?php
$l = 0;
$r = 0;
$ans = 0;
$q = 0;
$Q = 0;
$p = 0;
$w = array_fill(0, 99, 0);
$W = array_fill(0, 99, 0);

// Read input
$line = trim(fgets(STDIN));
if ($line === false || $line === '') {
    exit(0);
}
$parts = explode(' ', $line);
$l = (int)$parts[0];
$r = (int)$parts[1];

// Convert l to binary digits (least significant bit first)
$temp_l = $l;
while ($temp_l > 0) {
    $w[$q] = $temp_l % 2;
    $q++;
    $temp_l = intdiv($temp_l, 2);
}

// Convert r to binary digits (least significant bit first)
$temp_r = $r;
while ($temp_r > 0) {
    $W[$Q] = $temp_r % 2;
    $Q++;
    $temp_r = intdiv($temp_r, 2);
}

// Find the most significant bit where w and W differ
for ($i = $Q; $i >= 0; $i--) {
    if ($w[$i] != $W[$i]) {
        $p = $i + 1;
        break;
    }
}

// Calculate answer: (1 << p) - 1
// Since p can be up to 99, we need to handle large numbers
// PHP integers can handle up to 64 bits on 64-bit systems, but let's be safe
// Actually, the problem constraints likely keep p small enough for standard integers,
// but to be robust, we can use GMP if available, or just standard int if p < 63.
// Given the array size is 99, p can be up to 99.
// Standard PHP int is 64-bit. 2^99 exceeds 64-bit integer.
// However, looking at the C++ code, it uses `long long` (64-bit).
// If p > 63, `1ll << p` in C++ would be undefined or overflow.
// Assuming the input fits within 64-bit logic or the test cases don't exceed that.
// If we assume standard integer arithmetic is sufficient for the expected output range:
if ($p < 63) {
    $ans = (1 << $p) - 1;
} else {
    // Fallback for larger p if necessary, though unlikely in typical competitive programming with long long
    // Using GMP for safety if p is large
    $ans = gmp_sub(gmp_pow(2, $p), 1);
    $ans = gmp_strval($ans);
}

echo $ans;
?>

<?php
$fp_in = fopen('php://stdin', 'r');
$fp_out = fopen('php://stdout', 'w');

$l = (int)fread($fp_in, 1024);
$r = (int)fread($fp_in, 1024);

$w = array();
$W = array();
$q = 0;
$Q = 0;

while ($l > 0) {
    $w[$q] = $l % 2;
    $l = intdiv($l, 2);
    $q++;
}

while ($r > 0) {
    $W[$Q] = $r % 2;
    $r = intdiv($r, 2);
    $Q++;
}

$p = 0;
for ($i = $Q; $i >= 0; $i--) {
    if (!isset($w[$i])) {
        $w[$i] = 0;
    }
    if (!isset($W[$i])) {
        $W[$i] = 0;
    }
    if ($w[$i] != $W[$i]) {
        $p = $i + 1;
        break;
    }
}

$ans = (1 << $p) - 1;

fwrite($fp_out, $ans);

fclose($fp_in);
fclose($fp_out);
?>

define('INF', 2000000000);

function main() {
    $l = (int)trim(fgets(STDIN));

    $w = array();
    $W = array();
    $q = 0;
    $Q = 0;
    $p = 0;
    
    while ($l > 0) {
        $w[$q++] = $l % 2;
        $l = intdiv($l, 2);
    }
    
    while ($r > 0) {
        $W[$Q++] = $r % 2;
        $r = intdiv($r, 2);
    }
    
    for ($i = $Q; $i >= 0; $i--) {
        if (!isset($w[$i]) || !isset($W[$i]) || $w[$i] != $W[$i]) {
            $p = $i + 1;
            break;
        }
    }
    
    $ans = (1 << $p) - 1;
    echo $ans;
}

source_data.prob_desc_description: A little girl loves problems on bitwise operations very much. Here's one of them.You are given two integers l and r. Let's consider the values of  for all pairs of integers a and b (l ≤ a ≤ b ≤ r). Your task is to find the maximum value among all considered ones.Expression  means applying bitwise excluding or operation to integers x and y. The given operation exists in all modern programming languages, for example, in languages C++ and Java it is represented as "^", in Pascal — as "xor".
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: In a single line print a single integer — the maximum value of  for all pairs of integers a, b (l ≤ a ≤ b ≤ r).
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The single line contains space-separated integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 1018). Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in C++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
